title: You Needn't Have
gist_ar: مقال عن الفرق الدقيق بين الالتزام والاختيار في لغة الشغل.
text:
A manager who says "you might as well finish it today" has not given an
instruction, and both parties usually know it. The distinction matters, because a
great deal of workplace friction is a disagreement about modality rather than
about facts.

Consider four sentences an employee may hear. "You ought to have flagged this" is
a reproach about something no longer changeable. "You needn't have stayed late"
may well be gratitude, or it may be a criticism of judgement, and only tone
separates them. "You'd better speak to Legal" presents itself as advice while
carrying an implied consequence. And "you're supposed to log it within a day" is
the only one of the four that states an actual obligation, though it is the
mildest in form.

People are bound to read these inconsistently. An employee who is inclined to
caution treats every one of them as obligatory; one who is predisposed to
autonomy treats all four as advisable and no more. Neither is being unreasonable.
The necessity is genuinely unstated, and where it is unstated the reader supplies
it from temperament.

Managers reluctant to give direct instructions often believe they are extending
discretion. Frequently they are transferring risk. If the employee is not
entitled to know which of the four they are hearing, they cannot be held liable
for choosing wrongly, and yet invariably they are.

The remedy is unglamorous and it is not a policy. It is a habit: say whether a
thing is required, advisable, or merely available, and accept the constraint that
this places on you. A manager who cannot bear to be that explicit is not granting
freedom. They are declining to decide, and calling it trust.

questions.q: Which of the four sentences states a real obligation?
questions.q_ar: أنهي جملة من الأربعة بتعبّر عن إلزام حقيقي؟
options: You ought to have flagged this
You're supposed to log it within a day

questions.q: Why do employees read these sentences inconsistently?
questions.q_ar: ليه الموظفين بيفهموا الجمل دي بطرق مختلفة؟
options: They have not read the policy
The necessity is unstated, so they supply it from temperament

questions.q: What does the writer say indirect managers are often actually doing?
questions.q_ar: الكاتب بيقول إن المديرين غير المباشرين بيعملوا إيه فعلًا؟

questions.q: What is the writer's view of a manager who will not be explicit?
questions.q_ar: إيه رأي الكاتب في مدير مش عايز يكون واضح؟
options: They are respecting their staff's autonomy
They are declining to decide and calling it trust
